assets.subject: Low connected treeless foothills. Stable asset ID retained; no historical grove distribution implied.

A single compact cartographic landmark for the actual Jiumenkou water Great Wall in northern China, as weathered in the early 1920s. A straight old Chinese grey-stone fortified wall spanning a shallow river channel, with EXACTLY NINE separate side-by-side rectangular low water-gate openings below the wall, formed by EIGHT short wedge-shaped stone piers. All nine openings must be visible and countable from a near-frontal light-isometric angle. Modest crenellations above and two low Chinese brick bridgehead enclosures at opposite ends. One small weathered tiled gate tower. Rough pale stone riverbed, tiny visible water confined within the compact landmark; no long invented river course. Authentic Ming Chinese masonry, muted graphite stone with ochre light. No Roman aqueduct, western castle, rail track, train station, ornamental tourist landscaping, modern dam, intact modern reconstruction, tall exaggerated towers or vegetation slab. Transparent outside the complete landmark footprint. This is a stylized map symbol of the real structure, not a photoreal site reconstruction.
